practices_evaluation.practice_title: Responsible Addition of Test Code Maintenance
practices_evaluation.justification: The test interacts only with public API (constructor and numVertices()) and does not use reflection or access private state, indicating focus on observable behavior rather than implementation details.
The assertion is specific (assertEquals) but lacks a descriptive failure message. Only one assertion exists; no descriptive messages are present to aid debugging.
There is no commented-out test code or excessive trivial comments in the test method. Class-level comments are meaningful and explain traceability and intent.
Test uses fixed deterministic inputs (212) and no sources of non-determinism (random, time, Thread.sleep, external services) are used in the method body.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Complete Avoidance of Test Side Effects
practices_evaluation.justification: The test only creates an in-memory Grafo instance and does not persist data, modify static state, or require cleanup, so no side effects are introduced.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Suitable Utilization of Test Labels and Categories

The method performs two distinct 'Act' operations (insereAresta and retiraAresta). Decision rule 1: >1 act operations => non-compliant.
Test uses only local variables and no shared mutable state or execution-order naming; no @Before/@After needed to conclude independence.

Test is short (<10 lines), self-contained and does not repeat code within the class; no helper methods required for a single short test.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Rigorous Use of Performance and Security Tests
practices_evaluation.justification: No performance/security tests are expected in this unit test; no timeout-based performance or security-specific assertions are present.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Suitable Utilization of Test Labels and Categories
practices_evaluation.justification: Class is annotated with @Category(UnitTest.class), providing categorization for selective runs.

The test focuses on a single behavior: creating a graph, adding a self-edge, obtaining the transposed graph, and asserting identity/vertex counts. The Arrange (construct + insereAresta), Act (grafoTransposto) and Assert (assertNotSame and vertex counts) are a single coherent scenario testing the transpose behavior.

The method uses only local variables and does not rely on shared mutable state or other tests; no @Before/@After are required for this single test and there's no evidence of inter-test dependencies in the method body.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Coverage of Normal and Exceptional Flows
practices_evaluation.justification: Only a single happy-path scenario is present. There is no test for error conditions or exceptions (no assertThrows, no @Test(expected=...), and the class contains only this one test), so exceptional/error flows are not covered.

The test uses typical values (1165 and vertex 0) but does not exercise boundary values such as negative indices, index equal to numVertices, or empty/minimum sizes. No explicit boundary checks are present.

The single test is short and self-contained (< 10 lines). There are no duplicated blocks across multiple tests (only one test exists), and no obvious magic values repeated across methods that would require extraction.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Detailed Analysis of Size and Complexity
practices_evaluation.justification: The test method is small (< 20 lines) and linear, without loops or complex conditionals, indicating low cyclomatic complexity and a simple Arrange-Act-Assert flow.

The test contains multiple meaningful assertions (assertNotSame and two assertEquals) verifying different properties (distinct instances and vertex counts), providing multi-property verification rather than a single superficial assertion.
No @Ignore/@Disabled annotations or commented-out @Test methods are present in the provided method/class snippet. The test is active and runnable.
Class-level comments include Traceability entries referencing REQ-GRAFO-001 and REQ-GRAFO-002, which provides requirement IDs linked to the tests, satisfying traceability criteria for the method.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Rigorous Use of Performance and Security Tests
practices_evaluation.justification: This is a unit test that does not target performance or security concerns. There are no timing or security assertions in the method; per rules, performance/security testing is usually not applicable for such unit tests.
The test method name 'test8' is generic and does not describe the scenario or expected outcome. It does not follow descriptive naming conventions such as methodName_scenario_expectedBehavior.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Small Footprint of Test Code Generation
practices_evaluation.justification: The test uses EvoSuite runner/parameters and a numeric test name 'test8', which are indicators of generated tests. There are signs of tool-generated style (EvoRunner, EvoRunnerParameters and generic test naming).

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Complete Prioritization of Test Case Design
practices_evaluation.justification: The test appears to be a minimal happy-path check without explicit Given-When-Then structure or multiple scenarios showing prioritized design. The method lacks BDD-style comments or multiple scenario coverage to indicate thoughtful prioritization.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Responsible Addition of Test Code Maintenance
practices_evaluation.justification: The test interacts only with public Grafo API methods (constructor, insereAresta, grafoTransposto, numVertices) and does not access private fields or use reflection, indicating focus on public behavior rather than implementation details.

Assertions lack descriptive failure messages and, while multiple assertions exist, none include messages. The test uses assertEquals without messages and assertNotSame without a message, which reduces diagnostic clarity when failures occur.

There is no commented-out code within the method, and the class header includes purposeful comments explaining traceability and intent. The method itself is concise and does not suffer from excessive or misleading comments.
The method does not use randomness, current time, Thread.sleep, or external dependencies; it operates deterministically on in-memory Grafo instances, so results should be repeatable.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Complete Avoidance of Test Side Effects
practices_evaluation.justification: The test uses only local Grafo instances and does not persist data, modify static variables, create files, or leave open resources; there is no evidence of side effects that could affect other tests.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Suitable Utilization of Test Labels and Categories
practices_evaluation.justification: The class-level @Category(UnitTest.class) annotation is present, providing categorization for this test method and enabling selective execution, satisfying the labeling requirement.
